clue.text: Mad camper, man of a bygone era

indicators.note: something mad is crazed and disordered, so the letters of camper are jumbled

parts.note: Brian is a man's name, any man standing for a forename

explanation.surface: A crazed camper turns out to be a fellow from some long-vanished age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' is the anagram signal, and 'man' stands for any man's first name, a crossword habit; the comma hides that the definition is an adjective phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Precambrian is the geological eon before the Cambrian, so anything of it belongs to a vastly ancient time.

clue.text: Academy must have academic element!

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy, the London art institution
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: An exclamation that an academy simply must employ scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive gas, one of the chemical elements in the periodic table.

clue.text: Prisoner rendered excuse

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict
rendered means performed or carried out, i.e. done

explanation.surface: A prisoner offers some excuse for what he has done.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or forgive a wrong, a verb sense of excuse.

clue.text: I must go into battle at sea

indicators.note: the letter I must go inside the word for the battle, a containment instruction

parts.note: the Marne was a famous First World War battle in France

explanation.surface: A sailor insists that he must head into combat on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine describes things of or found in the sea, so it can stand for 'at sea' as an adjective.

clue.text: Journalist wants a half of real ale

indicators.note: taking a half of the word real keeps just its opening two letters

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, loosely an ale

explanation.surface: A newspaperman wants half a pint of real ale at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a half of' takes RE from REAL; a half is also a pub measure, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a newspaper or broadcast writer who gathers news, a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Putting up with a huge noise inside

indicators.note: the word for noise goes inside the word for huge

parts.note: huge means big
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone is tolerating a terrible racket within the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Abiding means tolerating or enduring, as in 'can't abide him', a synonym of putting up with.

clue.text: Welsh building has fancy hall with arches etc.

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Welsh edifice boasts an ornate hall with arches and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges HALL, ARCHES and ETC together.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlech Castle is a medieval fortress in Gwynedd, North Wales, built by Edward I.

clue.text: Big creature is around, on the loose

indicators.note: letters on the loose run free and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A huge beast is prowling around after escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the loose' fits the picture of an escaped beast, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is a prehistoric reptile, many of them enormous animals.

clue.text: Part amicably, having got to the end of the row?

definitions.text: having got to the end of the row?

explanation.surface: Two people separate on friendly terms after reaching the end of a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' here: a quarrel, not a line; at the end of an argument both sides accept their differences.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept disagreement is to separate in friendship, and it is also how a quarrel is ended without a winner.

clue.text: Shakespearean scene making one enthusiastic almost

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short of complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: ardent means passionate or enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare setting nearly makes one eager.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Arden is where much of As You Like It takes place, a Shakespearean setting.

clue.text: Mending material that's been given exposure to atmosphere

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
an airing is an exposure to fresh air

explanation.surface: Fixing up some fabric that has been hung out to air.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairing means fixing or restoring something broken, a synonym of mending.

clue.text: One with grounds ruined by darnel now

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A property holder whose fields are now spoilt by the weed darnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges DARNEL and NOW; darnel is a weedy grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who owns land has estates, i.e. grounds.

clue.text: Independent, with no people becoming united

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent, as of a politician
none means not one, no people at all

explanation.surface: A politician standing alone, with nobody joining him in union.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In one' means combined into a single whole, together.

clue.text: Tea permitted in holiday accommodation?

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Being allowed tea in a holiday cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin, often rented for vacations; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Paula's running around quietly before onset of extraordinary clapping etc

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the letter for quietly
running suggests the letters of the word with its S are moving about into a fresh order

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction meaning quietly

indicators.note: onset of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Paula is jogging softly round before an outstanding ovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges PAULAS to APLAUS; 'around' puts P inside, giving APPLAUS; 'onset of' takes E from extraordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is the clapping and cheering of an approving audience.

clue.text: Star sporting grand tie

indicators.note: sporting can mean playful or frolicking, so the letters play about into a new order

explanation.surface: A celebrity wearing a showy necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large, cool, late-stage star such as Betelgeuse.

clue.text: Impoverished country expelling a well-to-do man

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so the letter a is removed from the country

parts.note: India is a country
a gent is a gentleman, a man of good standing

explanation.surface: A poor nation throwing out a wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelling' drops the A at the end of INDIA, leaving INDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy or poor, lacking the necessities of life.

clue.text: Building slab al brought across street

indicators.note: the gangster's surname is brought across the street abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Someone named Al carries a building slab over the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'al' is Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, whose surname is spread around ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstone is a stone placed on top of a wall or structure, a crowning slab.

clue.text: Winged sandals are the content of a sentimental aria by Puccini

indicators.note: the answer is contained within the following words, running across two of them

explanation.surface: Winged footwear is the subject of a sentimental Puccini aria.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across sentimenTAL ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Talaria are the winged sandals of Hermes (Mercury) in Greek and Roman myth.

clue.text: Disgusting place at the front, clear at the back

parts.note: to place is to put
to rid is to clear of something

explanation.surface: A revolting spot at the front, though tidied at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the front' and 'at the back' just say which piece goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrid means rotten and foul-smelling, so revolting.

clue.text: Bring to light a Parisian with a broken heart

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: broken means the word heart is smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with a broken heart reveals all.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to dig up or discover, revealing something hidden.

clue.text: Difficult situation in filthy place that is restricting millions

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the pieces enclose the abbreviation for millions

parts.note: a sty is a pigpen, any filthy place
ie is id est, Latin for that is
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Being stuck in a grimy hole that is holding millions.
explanation.definitionFit: A stymie is an obstacle or predicament, originally a golf ball blocking the line to the hole.

clue.text: Playwright has left behind item of clothing

indicators.note: behind means the abbreviation for left comes after the playwright

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: A dramatist has abandoned a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl is a piece of fabric worn over the shoulders, a garment.

clue.text: At home the expert is totally exposed

parts.note: in means at home
taken as written
a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: An expert at home is entirely laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means naked, with skin uncovered.

clue.text: Illegally take old city, protected by American power

indicators.note: the old city is guarded by the pieces around it

parts.note: US means American
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Seizing an ancient city shielded by American might.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize a throne or power without right.

clue.text: Powerful ray alarms bee in flight

indicators.note: in flight suggests the letters buzzing about and landing in a new order

explanation.surface: A bee flying around causes alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a narrow concentrated light emission, an intense ray.

clue.text: The way to get energy after heavy defeat

indicators.note: after means the energy abbreviation comes behind the defeat

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: How to regain vigour after a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a road or course to follow, a way.

clue.text: The main defenders of Britons' freedom from slavery?

definitions.text: The main defenders of Britons' freedom from slavery?

parts.words: The main defenders of Britons' freedom from slavery?
parts.note: main is the sea; Rule, Britannia! says Britannia rules the waves and Britons never shall be slaves, so the defenders are warships

explanation.surface: Who are chief protectors of British liberty against servitude?
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'chief' but is the old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Large armoured warships were for centuries the Royal Navy's guard of Britain's shores.
